title: Operator interference and the degeneracy among L2, L4, L9-L12 and L16: what a second event (and a tenth) would distinguish
question: Which lone-event-compatible NR operators (O6, O10, O9, O14, O15, O5v, L10, O9xq^2; inelastic O1/O4 at delta = 300-380 keV) are spectrally degenerate in xenon, how many events separate each pair at 3 sigma with LZ resolution and the 600 vs 1000 phd edge, can O1+O6 or O4+O6 interference hide an SI/SD admixture in a lone 248 keV event, and what does a second event's energy tell?
headline_result: Only O9/O14 (~3000 events), isoscalar/isovector Sigma'' pairs (>1e4) and mass >= 400 GeV (>= 250) are truly degenerate; O6 = E_R x O10 exactly (same Sigma'' response, one power of q^2 apart) separates with 15-20 events, L10 from O6 or O9xq^2 with 30-60, elastic from inelastic with 2-7; O1+O6 is exactly incoherent and the low-energy null bounds the O1 share of the high-energy rate to <= 1e-3 (sigma_n <= 1-2e-47 cm^2 at 1 TeV)
key_numbers: ratios: O6/O10 ~ E^0.9995 (0.0006 dex), O9/O14 slope 0.08 (0.007 dex), L10/(O9 q^2) ~ E^-1.002, O6s/O6v H=0.008; N_3sigma toys (LZ/1000 phd): O6-O10 20/15-20, L10-O6 30-40/40-50, L10-O9q2 40-60, O6-O5v 60-80, L10-inel366 2-7/2-5, inel366-380 10-15/20-40; Gaussian O9-O14 3650/2520, O6s-O6v 17100/12900, 400 GeV vs 1 TeV >= 250; median of 36 elastic pairs 20; O1+O6 incoherent to 4e-16, O4+O6 cross term ~ q^2 Sigma'' (node 3.60 MeV x c4/c6); hidden O1 (N_lo<=3/5): f_hi <= 9.1e-4/1.6e-3, c1/c6 <= 1.5/1.9e-5, sigma_n <= 1.2/2.1e-47 cm^2; |c4/c6| <= 0.016, O4 share <= 6-17%; second-event LR vs L10 (1000 phd): E2=100 keV inelastic <= 0.04, E2=248 elastic 0.34-1.45, E2=350 inel366/380 6.0/7.4; Sun-frame vs annual halo N_3sigma 47-98 (delta 366), 5.5 (380)
model_or_mechanism: NREFT spin-1/2 operators in xenon (WimPyDD shell-model responses); observed-energy pdfs with erf efficiency edges (E50 = 269.9 or 423.2 keV) and sigma_E = 11 sqrt(E/248) keV; KL/Hellinger distances, Gaussian and toy-MC N_3sigma, hierarchical clustering; two-operator Hamiltonians with response cross terms; second-event likelihood-ratio lookup
confidence: high for response-level ratios and interference checks (machine precision, coupling-independent); medium for N_3sigma (1D observed-energy proxy, KL floor, assumed 1000 phd roll-off width)
